newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares nudge higher, track Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares nudge higher, track Wall Street.

text.p: Philippine shares finished higher on Tuesday buoyed by the overnight rise in U.S. shares but turnover was thin, traders said.
"The market closed up but this might just be a technical rebound since volume is not that big," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities Inc.
Main index closed 16.62 points, or 0.57 percent, at 2,949.46 points.
"Market closed up led by the Dow," Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc, said, adding that there was bargain hunting in selected blue chips.
All indices rose except for the mining sector. Decliners slightly outnumbered gainers 47 to 44 with 97 issues unchanged.
Benpres Holdings Corp held its gains at close which traders attributed to news it had divested stakes in its media subsidiaries allowing direct foreign investment in Benpres.

Property stocks Empire East Land Holdings Inc and Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc suffered selldown in late trade on lingering concern the companies were suffering financial problems, traders said.
"The public perception is that they are illiquid despite the company dispelling such rumours," said Russell Ong, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.

Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc earlier denied it is suffering financial difficulties along with unit Empire saying that for the first quarter of 1997 alone, Megaworld expects a 36 percent rise in net ncome to 500 million pesos.

Asiamerit's Lee said the market would continue to track the Dow on Wednesday. She said the rise in the 91-day treasury bill rates would continue to divert attention away from the equities market. - KATHERINE ESPINA 63 2 841-8939 Fax 8176267
